name: Microsoft Agent Framework
summary: Multi-language (.NET, Python, Go) library for building agents and graph-based multi-agent workflows, positioned as the successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel. Provides agents, sessions, context providers, middleware, MCP clients, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and an evaluation framework, with optional Microsoft Foundry hosting.

agent-runtime.note: Agent abstraction with streaming and non-streaming runs, AgentSession state management, history providers, and middleware for intercepting agent actions.

orchestration.note: Graph-based and functional workflows with sequential, concurrent, handoff, and group-chat patterns plus checkpointed long-running runs.

knowledge-memory.note: Sessions and context/history providers give conversational and long-term memory, but document ingestion and vector search come from external providers such as Mem0.

tools-integration.note: Function tools plus first-class MCP clients (stdio, streamable HTTP, websocket) and hosted MCP tools across Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Ollama.

identity-governance.note: Per-tool human approval with standing and auto-approval rules is built in, but there is no IAM, quota, or audit-log subsystem.

observability.note: Emits OpenTelemetry traces, logs, and metrics per the GenAI semantic conventions, including token usage and per-tool invocation duration.

data-secrets.note: No managed file storage or encrypted secrets service; credentials come from Azure identity or environment variables.

evaluation.note: Built-in evaluation framework with evaluators and results, local checks (keyword, tool-called, custom functions), and Foundry model-as-judge evaluators.

channels.note: DevUI provides a web chat interface with an OpenAI-compatible API, but it is an explicitly non-production sample app and there are no messaging-platform gateways.

code-execution.note: Code Interpreter is a provider-side hosted tool whose availability depends on the model provider; no local sandbox runtime ships with the framework.
